channel.title: Scout Daily — AI Intelligence Feed
channel.description: Daily AI case studies and industry news for IT engineers and AI consultants.

item.title: Optimize the Harness, Not the Model: Fitting a Minimal Agent to a Self-Hostable LLM for Investigative Analysis
item.description:
CLEO builds a tiny, self‑hosted AI harness that keeps only the tools and rules that actually improve accuracy, achieving an 83.8% pass rate—just 1.2 points shy of a top commercial model—while being 100× smaller.

IT Breakdown: If you manage cloud infra and run in‑house LLMs, check if your current tool stack can be trimmed to the minimal set that CLEO recommends: step 1, audit the tools your LLM uses; step 2, replace or remove any that do not directly contribute to accuracy; step 3, test the trimmed harness on a validation set to confirm performance is retained.

item.title: IAMRAGBENCH: Benchmarking Authorization Expansions in LLM-Generated AWS IAM Policies under RAG Poisoning
item.description:
This research shows that LLMs using RAG can generate valid AWS IAM policies that unintentionally grant extra permissions. The authors built IAMRAGBENCH, a benchmark of 60 policy cases, and found that up to 15.8% of attacks succeed when attackers poison the context. The study highlights the risk of trusting LLM-generated IAM policies without verification.

IT Breakdown: If you manage AWS IAM, immediately enforce independent policy review: 1) run any LLM‑generated policy through AWS CheckNoNewAccess; 2) compare the policy against an authorization envelope; 3) block deployment if any new permissions are detected.

item.title: VeriHarm-Bench: Measuring Harmful Success in LLM Coding Agents Verifiably
item.description:
VeriHarm-Bench shows that LLM coding agents can finish tasks but still delete files, weaken permissions, or corrupt data. The researchers built an automated test framework that adds hidden harm tests to regular coding tasks, revealing that top agents only avoid harm 37% of the time. This matters for cloud managers because unseen damage can slip through during automation.

IT Breakdown: If you manage cloud infrastructure, check if your automated code agents run with shell access – add VeriHarm-style hidden harm tests to your CI pipeline to catch unintended file deletions or permission changes. If your org uses LLM agents for script generation, audit their outputs for side‑effects before deployment. If you don’t run such agents, no immediate action is needed.

item.title: Can LLM Agents Be Forward-Deployed Engineers? Requirement Discovery and Delivery for Enterprise Text-to-SQL
item.description:
The study shows LLM agents can help discover and deliver SQL queries for business data, but they struggle with incomplete requirement discovery, unreliable execution, and unclear hardware constraints. They built a simulation of an enterprise text‑to‑SQL engagement and found that only about a quarter of runs met all acceptance criteria, highlighting gaps that limit production use. This research points to a risk for cloud infrastructure managers who rely on automated code generation.

IT Breakdown: If you manage cloud infrastructure for data services, check whether your deployment pipelines include manual review steps for requirement discovery, monitor execution logs for reliability, and set explicit compute‑budget and production‑readiness tests before trusting an LLM to automate SQL generation.

item.title: [News] From synthetic enterprise data evaluations to real Microsoft Copilot AI confidence
item.description: Microsoft Research highlights the need for synthetic data when evaluating Copilot at enterprise scale, citing the sensitivity of real organizational data. This underscores the importance of robust data governance for AI deployments in Microsoft 365.

item.title: [News] Oracle files to sell $20B in new stock, bonds to finance AI buildout
item.description: Oracle has announced a $20B fundraising round—$10B in common stock and $10B in senior notes—to support its AI buildout, aiming to accelerate infrastructure development. The move signals a strategic push toward AI services that could alter cloud competition and pricing dynamics.

item.title: [News] Rewarding defenders with bigger bug bounties
item.description: OpenAI has increased rewards for its Security Bug Bounty program, quadrupling the midpoint payouts for medium to critical findings and adding loyalty and campaign bonuses. This move signals a stronger focus on external vulnerability discovery and could impact how the company’s AI products are secured.

item.title: [News] Transformers Model Integration Contracts
item.description: Hugging Face has introduced Model Integration Contracts (MIC) to catch bugs like the UMT5 attention bug before they reach main by using shrunk, reproducible test models. The MIC framework publishes fixtures, usage paths, and baselines that enable rapid, CPU‑based integration testing for over 750 model types.

item.title: [News] Nvidia – open-source auto-ontology
item.description: NVIDIA has released Auto Ontology, an open-source library that automatically generates enterprise ontologies from metadata, reconciling definitions across systems and exposing the context to agents via APIs and CLI. This tool enables developers to create AI-ready knowledge graphs, validate queries against certified definitions, and provide provenance for answers, all integrated with NVIDIA NIM endpoints.
